title: Active Data is editable outside the governance cycles, but the rules for editing it are not
content:
A.1.13.1.1 explains why an exception is needed: Active Data documents "must be maintained and frequently updated as part of the Sky Ecosystem's routine operational tasks," and so "can be directly modified outside of the standard Weekly Governance Cycle and Monthly Governance Cycle."

The control comes from a second document. Each Active Data document has an associated **Active Data Controller** document defining exactly two elements: "the 'Responsible Party', or the entity who is obligated to update the Active Data, and... the 'Update Process', or the authorized process by which the Active Data is updated."

The load-bearing asymmetry is stated twice, in A.1.13.1.2 and A.1.13.1.3: because both elements live in the Controller, modifying *who* may update the data or *how* they may do it "is subject to a SKY vote pursuant to standard governance processes" — per the annotation at A.1.13.1.2.0.3.1, via the Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle, Atlas Edit Monthly Cycle, Bootstrapping Governance Poll, or Operational Weekly Cycle.

This is a clean separation of data from policy, and it is what makes fast operational mutation safe. Governance never votes on the current value of a list; it votes once on who is trusted to maintain that list and by what procedure, then lets them work at operational speed. A.1.13.1.3 tightens it further by requiring every Update Process to "conform to one of the processes defined in the subdocuments herein" — Controllers select from a fixed menu rather than inventing bespoke procedures.

The residual risk is that the vote-gated layer is only as strong as the boundary between data and policy. Anything smuggled into an Active Data document escapes voting entirely, so classification of a document as Active Data is itself a governance decision with real consequences.
description: Each Active Data document has a Controller document naming a Responsible Party and an Update Process; the data changes freely while the Controller requires a SKY vote to change.
